British Values
The Government set out its definition of British values in the 2011 Prevent Strategy, and these values were reiterated in (2014) with the Department of Education reinforcing the need “to create and enforce a clear and rigorous expectation on all schools to promote the fundamental British values of democracy, the rule of law, individual liberty and mutual respect and tolerance of those with different faiths and beliefs”.
We aim to work closely with our parents, other schools and organisations, building partnerships, which benefit, not only our children, but others in the wider community, both on a local, national and global level. We have interwoven our British Values into our Islamic values and UNCRC treaty.
At Quwwat ul Islam Girls’ School, we ensure that core Islamic and British values are reinforced regularly and in the following ways:
Pupil Voice is firmly embedded in the ethos of our school, and the children have many opportunities for their voices to be heard.
Our School Council is just one example:
School council elections are held at the beginning of each year, and all children in Years 1 to 11 are invited to stand. A councillor is elected from each class to represent the opinions, suggestions and issues raised from the class. School Council meetings are held twice a term and are led by the Head teacher, Mrs Member.
Quwwat ul Islam Girls’ School is currently in the process of achieving the bronze award towards the UNICEF Rights Respecting School Award. Each year the children decide upon their “class charter”, as well as the rights associated with these and all children contribute to the drawing up of their individual class charters.
The importance of laws, whether they be those that govern the class, the school, or the country, are consistently reinforced throughout regular school days, as well as when dealing with behaviour and through school assemblies. Pupils are taught the value and reasons behind laws, that they govern and protect us, the responsibilities that this involves and the consequences when laws are broken. Visits from authorities such as the Police and Fire Service help reinforce this message.
Within school, pupils are actively encouraged to make choices and take responsibility for these choices, knowing that they are in a safe and supportive environment. As a school we have a responsibility to provide boundaries and safety for children through rules and regulations but also to give our children opportunities to make mistakes and to learn from their experiences.
Pupils are encouraged to know, understand and exercise their rights and personal freedoms and advised how to exercise these safely, for example, through E-Safety lessons.
Whether it be through their choice of learning challenges, how they record a piece of learning, or through participation in our range of extra-curricular clubs and opportunities, pupils are given the freedom to make choices.
Through our curriculum and the QUIGS Learning Drivers (Caring for Ourselves, Caring for Our World, Caring for Our Education and Caring for Our Rights) children are provided with the opportunity to develop through each learning driver by achieving the individual character development strands.
We also encourage a community spirit and sense of belonging, where children show respect for each other, understand differences and have a very clear sense of right and wrong. Children learn that their behaviour impacts on their own rights and those of others. All members of the school community are expected to treat each other with respect.
When children leave QUIGS, they do so not only as enthusiastic and learners, but also as responsible and caring young people with an understanding of their role as part of a community.
Tolerance of those of Different Faiths and Beliefs
Our programme of assemblies address understanding and acceptance of different faiths and beliefs through stories and celebrations from a variety of faiths and cultures. R.E, PSHE and RRSA teaching reinforce this. In RE lessons, members of different faiths or religions are encouraged to share their knowledge to enhance learning within classes and the school and classes visit places of worship that are important to different faiths.
Open Evenings, Drop Down days and Achievement assemblies together with annual events such as the Summer Fete are just a sample of some of the significant dates in the school calendar, which are always well-supported and enjoyed by pupils, families, staff and members of the wider community.

Assalamualaikum, Welcome to Quwwat-ul-Islam Girls’ School
Quwwat-ul-Islam Girls’ School was established in August 2003. Initially, the school enrolled just fifty pupils but over time, by the Grace of Allah, the school expanded and has gone from strength to strength. In September 2005, the school was extended to cater for Secondary pupils.
We now cater for pupils from Reception to the Year 11, teaching the National Curriculum Subjects, as well as providing a solid Islamic education within a nurturing Islamic environment.
The Islamic Studies Curriculum aims to instill the light of the Prophetic guidance within the hearts of our students. The curriculum is delivered in a caring environment to help nurture our future generations in becoming confident young Muslim women ready for life in modern day Britain. We aim to develop student’s acquisition of the core knowledge of our religion in accordance with the Quran and Sunnah. Students will be empowered to take personal responsibility for themselves, their environment and of others within the wider community, ultimately as true flag bearers of the Ummah.
Narrated Abu Hurairah: that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: “Whoever takes a path upon which to obtain knowledge, Allah makes the path to Paradise easy for him.”
— Jami` at-Tirmidhi 2646
Quwwat-ul-Islam Girls’ School celebrates diversity and welcomes applications from children of all faiths and backgrounds.
Quwwat-ul-Islam Girls’ School thanks all of its past and current parents for their continuous support and cooperation.

Careers
Post 16 Pathways
At Quwwat – ul – Islam Girls’ School, we work closely with our local authority, Newham Council , to ensure that all Year 11 students receive clear, structured and supportive guidance when planning their Post-16 pathways. The transition from Year 11 to further education, training or employment is an important stage in every student’s journey, and our school is committed to ensuring that pupils are fully informed about the wide range of opportunities available to them.
Through the support and guidance provided by the Newham Council Post-16 team, students are introduced to a variety of progression routes, including A-Level study, vocational and technical courses, T-Levels, apprenticeships and further education pathways. This guidance is delivered through a collaborative approach between the council and local schools, helping students understand the qualifications, entry requirements and future career opportunities linked to each pathway.
At Quwwat – ul – Islam, we integrate this guidance into our careers programme and personal development curriculum, ensuring that students begin exploring their options early in Year 11. The school facilitates assemblies, workshops and one-to-one guidance opportunities, enabling students to hear directly from colleges, sixth forms and training providers. These sessions help pupils make informed decisions about their next steps and understand what different Post-16 settings expect from applicants.
As part of this partnership work, key local providers such as Newham College, New City College , Leyton College Sixth Form and many more, regularly engage with our students through in-school presentations, application workshops, careers events and open-day opportunities. These interactions allow students to explore different learning environments, ask questions about courses, and gain a clearer understanding of the pathways available after GCSEs.
At Quwwat – ul – Islam Girls’ School, our priority is to ensure that every student feels confident, prepared and supported when choosing their Post-16 destination. By working closely with the Newham Council and local education providers, we provide students with the knowledge, guidance and encouragement needed to progress successfully into further education, training or employment, enabling them to pursue ambitions that reflect their interests, strengths and long-term goals.

RSE/Relationship Education
How is RSE and Relationship Education taught at Quwwat ul Islam Girls’ School?
At Quwwat ul Islam Girls’ School we believe that the teaching of RSE and Relationship Education is vital in order to help our students to embrace the challenges of creating a happy and successful adult life. We believe that all our pupils need to have the knowledge that will enable them to make informed decisions about their wellbeing, health and relationships.
Pupils can also put this knowledge into practice as they develop the capacity to make sound decisions when facing risks, challenges and complex situations. The topics covered in the RSE and Re Curriculum can help support young people to develop resilience, to know how and when to ask for help, and to know where to access support.
We strongly believe that high quality, evidence-based and age-appropriate teaching of RSE and RE can help prepare pupils for the opportunities, responsibilities and experiences of adult life. They can also enable us to promote the spiritual, moral, social, cultural, mental and physical development of our pupils.
At QUIGS we have chosen to implement a curriculum specially designed by, The Association of Muslim Schools (AMS), a curriculum which is:

SEND at Quwwatul Islam Girls School
At Quwwatul Islam Girls School we strongly believe that every child has the right to high quality education that can help them achieve their potential, regardless of their starting point. We are an inclusive school, we use a number of approaches to teaching that support all children and their different learning styles.
Message from our SENCO
As the SENCO at Quwwatul Islam Girls’ School, I am beyond thrilled to have been given this position and feel honoured and happy to join such a motivating and supportive institution.
I have nine years of teaching experience and am a certified Special Educational Needs Coordinator. I’ve received praise from our Newham area SENCO for introducing new ideas and putting into practise interactive activities that are open to all children with support from our Newham area SENCO.
In order to assist your child’s educational and wellbeing needs, I will be working closely with parents and taking on board your views and thoughts. For parents with SEND needs I hold termly review meetings and hold monthly SEND Surgeries where parents and carers are welcome to attend and discuss any matters they may have regarding their child’s learning.
We also have a great team working closely to support children with educational needs through our intervention programs daily.

RWI Phonics
Right from the beginning of Reception, we use Read Write Inc. Phonics which is a highly successful English programme.
The Read Write Inc. Phonics programme is carefully matched to the curriculum, giving every child at Quwwat-Ul-Islam Girls’ school the best chance of success.
The programme helps children learn to read fluently and at speed so that they can focus on developing their skills in comprehension, vocabulary and spelling. The programme is designed for children aged 4-7. However, we will continue teaching RWI to children beyond the age of 7 if they still need support in their reading.
